criteria.quote: "Charizard looks tiny beside its own form."
criteria.revision: Remove the unsupported size claim. The research does not provide either height, weight, or Gigantamax size. Open instead with a sourced contrast: "Charizard has a Gigantamax variety—but unlike Mega X, it stays Fire/Flying."

criteria.quote: "Gigantamax Charizard grows from 1.7 meters to 28 meters, over sixteen times its normal height."
criteria.revision: The measurements are not supported by the supplied research, so do not build the story around them. Make it uniquely Charizard through its documented forms: Charizard Gmax is Fire/Flying, Mega Y is Fire/Flying, and Mega X is Fire/Dragon.

criteria.quote: "What makes Charizard look tiny beside its own form?"
criteria.revision: The question promises an explanation, but the draft only answers with a measurement. Replace it with a source-backed open loop: "Why does one of Charizard’s special forms change its type while the others do not?"

criteria.quote: "Its Gigantamax form weighs a full one thousand kilograms."
criteria.revision: Cut the unsupported weight scene; it neither follows from nor deepens the opening question. Escalate through the documented form reveal: first establish Charizard as Fire/Flying, then reveal Mega Y remains Fire/Flying, then reveal Mega X alone is Fire/Dragon.

criteria.quote: "Gigantamax Charizard stands twenty-eight meters tall, not one point seven."
criteria.revision: The size reveal is unsupported by the research. Use the stronger supported reversal instead: reveal that Gigantamax Charizard does not change from Fire/Flying, while Mega X does become Fire/Dragon.

criteria.quote: "Charizard looks tiny beside its own form." / "Gigantamax Charizard stands twenty-eight meters tall, not one point seven." / "More than sixteen normal Charizards reach from ground to its head."
criteria.revision: These scenes repeat the same scale point, and all depend on unsupported measurements. Replace them with distinct facts: Charizard is Fire/Flying; Charizard Gmax is Fire/Flying; Mega Y is Fire/Flying; Mega X is Fire/Dragon.

criteria.quote: "At 28 meters, Gigantamax Charizard towers over a stack of sixteen normal Charizards."
criteria.revision: This only restates the premise and is unsupported by the research. Pay off the revised type-change setup with: "Gigantamax makes Charizard a different variety without changing its Fire/Flying type. Mega X is the form that changes Charizard into Fire/Dragon."

criteria.quote: "Which feels like Charizard: 1.7-meter flier or 28-meter giant?"
criteria.revision: Both size descriptions are unsupported, so the split cannot be grounded in the supplied research. Ask a credible form-based split instead: "Which is the bigger change to Charizard: becoming Gigantamax while staying Fire/Flying, or becoming Mega X and gaining Dragon type?"
